scope: Independent immutable-output audit of 16 gain/bias restorations, 2 nominal/identity controls and 12 COM/inertia-group restorations; no simulation stepping, model changes, training, installation, or hardware access.

verdict.conclusion: Fresh nominal and identity-transfer controls settle. All 16 gain/bias cases and all 4 COM-only cases fail the final sampled quiet screen. Restoring nominal body mass, central principal inertia and inertial-frame quaternion jointly produces 4/4 quiet cases conditional on zero bias, unit gains and captured material; adding nominal COM also produces 4/4. These conditional parameter-group effects do not identify a unique mass, limb, central-inertia, or interaction cause, and do not validate hardware or a new policy.

limitations: Only two startup worlds selected posthoc and two material assumptions; counts are descriptive, not population reliability estimates.

Mass+inertia restoration changes all 13 bodies and three fields together. It is not an isolated mass-only, limb-only, or tensor-only intervention. Principal inertia and inertial-frame quaternion must be interpreted together.
All 12 inertial interventions are conditional on zero encoder bias and unit gain scales; no claim that restoring this group alone resolves the original biased/gain-scaled baseline.
Synthetic identity and restorations retain original donor-capture provenance; their edited tables are not observed GPU/hardware values.

Quiet screen is descriptive: every selected last 0.5 s sample below .02 m/s body planar speed, .05 rad/s worldheading difference and every joint below .05 rad/s.26 state samples span25/52 s; the 8 s command tail has 416 saved states spanning415/52 s. No continuous-time stability claim.

WorldXY interval speeds and instantaneous body-plane speeds are distinct; both give the same verdict in all 30 cases. World yaw uses unwrapped quaternion-derived heading differences, not body angular velocity.

State is recorded after one 520 Hz step while time_s and contact samples refer to prestep; constant1/520 s offset cancels intervals. 52 Hz sampled torque/contact checks cannot establish unsampled behavior; literal model force cap is 3 Nm.
Fixed 16 ms delay, 520 Hz physics, 52 Hz inference and initialization/fade are inspected source contracts. This audit does not replay 520 Hz physics or reconstruct missing delay samples.
Exactly 25 watched source files agree with their stated Git commits and each other; this is not a complete hash of every transitive dependency.
No robot, hardware calibration estimate, installed-policy change, model modification, or new simulation/training was performed.
